subject: HelixAI evaluation — compact recommendations, benchmark proofs, and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kaur <samir@helixai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixAI evaluation — compact recommendations, benchmark proofs, and next steps

Samir / Helix team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great discussion on the real-time summarization use case and the latency/throughput targets you shared (p99 < 220ms for short queries, burst TPS up to ~320). I promised a short follow-up with concrete model recommendations and links to the Redwood-verified benchmark artifacts we ran against a dataset close to your payload.

Compact recs (first pass)
- Recommendation A (balanced): vicuna-13b-rlhf-quantized — best tradeoff for your mix of short prompts + occasional long contexts; median latency ~60ms on a g4dn-like instance with Redwood batching and prefix cache enabled.
- Recommendation B (low-latency): redwood-turbo-7b-fp16 — lower latency p50/p90 on small-context queries, good for interactive UX; expect slightly lower quality on long-context summarization.
- Recommendation C (quality guardrail): openchat-34b (cpu-offload optimized) — highest baseline quality on long threads, but requires different scaling economics.

What we ran and where to look
- Redwood-verified performance profile (TPS, p50/p90/p99): https://app.redwood.ai/perf/helixai/2027-04-22
- Raw TPS + latency CSV snapshot (attached): helix_eval_tps_snapshot.csv
- Prompt pack we used (short/long prompt variants, few-shot examples): prompt-pack-v3.txt

Quality/regression notes
- We saw model-specific degradation on prompts that rely on long-chain coreference; for vicuna-13b we captured a small set of failing cases (included in Drive folder) — recommend adding the short prompt guardrail (truncate + head-context) to keep p99 latency steady without quality regressions.
- Prefix/KV cache sensitivity: enabling plan-cache for repeated conversation prefixes reduced per-token CPU by ~18% in our runs; we'll include recommended cache TTLs in the pilot config.

Next steps (suggested, quick)
1) Agree pilot scope: 3k daily queries, traffic split: 60% vicuna-13b, 30% redwood-turbo-7b, 10% openchat-34b fallback.
2) Grant us read-only access to a small sample of production traces (anonymized) for final prompt tuning (secure share or HubSpot link).
3) Schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff with infra + procurement to lock on contract/throughput SLAs (I suggested availability next Thu 10–11am PT).

I cc'd Rishi and Tessa to add perf/server-side details and an initial pilot config.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Attachment: helix_eval_tps_snapshot.csv (CSV · 48KB)
Attachment: prompt-pack-v3.txt (text · 12KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI evaluation — compact recommendations, benchmark proofs, and next steps

Grace / Samir — quick add from infra side with more granular numbers and pilot knobs.

Bench highlights (from the run attached)
- vicuna-13b-rlhf-quantized @ batch_size=8: p50=58ms, p90=102ms, p99=218ms under steady-state 220 TPS; sustained TPS with continuous batching ~280 TPS before latency SLO drift.
- redwood-turbo-7b-fp16 @ batch_size=4: p50=32ms, p90=68ms, p99=145ms — excellent for short-turn latency.
- openchat-34b: p50=210ms, p90=430ms, p99=980ms (recommend as fallback for long-run offline jobs rather than interactive).

Operational knobs we recommend for pilot
- Auto-balance routing policy: route by latency SLO with warm fallback to redwood-turbo-7b when queue depth > 12 requests. This keeps interactive UX consistent while preserving quality for high-compute items.
- KV cache TTL: 45s for repeated conversation prefixes (your traffic shows short sessions); reduce to 8s for high-variance flows.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic for first 48 hrs, monitor error-rate and quality regressions via eval prompts (we'll ship a small prompt-check endpoint to run daily).

I'll attach the per-model kernel-selection trace and a simple pilot config snippet — see Drive link in Grace's email. If Helix wants, we can pre-seed the pilot config into a dedicated cluster so you see a turnkey trial.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Grace / Rishi — really helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock scope: 

1) On vicuna-13b: the p99 you quoted sits close to our p99 target (220ms). How stable was that p99 across runs (we care about tail variance during 2x traffic spikes)?
2) For the prompt-pack: can you flag the exact few-shot templates you used for the long-context summarization tests? Our product team will want to reproduce locally.
3) Procurement asked for a pilot pricing estimate and the minimal commit we should expect — can you send a ballpark for the three-model mixed-slate you proposed?

Agree on a 30-min kickoff next Thu — can we do 10:30am PT instead of 10am? Also happy to give a small sample of anonymized traces; I'll share via the Drive folder you linked.

Subject: Re: HelixAI evaluation — compact recommendations, benchmark proofs, and next steps

Samir — perfect, thanks for the follow-up questions. Answers and next artifacts below.

1) p99 stability: we reran the vicuna-13b profile across three 45-minute windows with traffic shaped to 1x and 2x (approx. 220 TPS and ~440 TPS). p99 moved from 218ms -> 245ms under the 2x synthetic spike when KV cache was disabled; with recommended cache TTL=45s and the routing policy in place, p99 tightened to ~230–235ms. We'll include the variance graph in the Drive folder; link above.

2) prompt-pack specifics: the few-shot templates used for long-context summarization live in prompt-pack-v3.txt (section "long_thread_templates"). I highlighted the exact templates and the sampling seeds so your product team can reproduce.

3) pilot pricing (ballpark)
- Estimated monthly pilot cost (dev/staging cluster, 3k daily queries, mix described): $8,500–$12,000/mo depending on autoscale bursts.
- Minimal committed reserved slots to keep p99 ~230ms during burst: equivalent of 4 dedicated g4dn-like workers (we'll translate to your cloud SKU in the kickoff).

Pilot kickoff: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:30am PT — I sent a calendar invite separately (includes Zoom + agenda). During the kickoff we'll: confirm contract owner on your side, share a pre-seeded pilot config, and enable the daily prompt-check endpoint so product can watch the first 48-hour regression indicators.

I'll also open an internal ticket to surface a short SLA addendum for the pilot (can share as a one-pager). If procurement wants a formal statement-of-work, we can attach the pilot config + bench snapshots to that doc.

Looking forward to it — thanks again.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
